subject: shiny server on Ubuntu package error

messages.author: 2bf707539ac457df
messages.subject: shiny server on Ubuntu package error
parts:
Am running shiny server on ubuntu 14.04TLS. I have also R base running on the same machine. I've put a wordcloud  app in the "/var/shiny-server/www" directory. Other apps are aslo there also in the directory.  I can server all apps on my intranet from shiny server. However, the wordcloud app can not be served with shiny server. I get an error that state a specific package ("tm")can not be located.  When opening terminal and running the app with 'runApp("wordCloud") from the same server, the app works fine - it doesn't complain the tm package not being there.

So, the question is why am I not able to have the "tm" package not found when serving the app via the shinny server - while on the same machine I can run the app from console....

Confirming the package lib is attached...

> installed.packages()[,1]
       memoise            NLP   RColorBrewer          shiny           slam
     "memoise"          "NLP" "RColorBrewer"        "shiny"         "slam"
            tm      wordcloud         digest      htmltools         httpuv


Here is the error I see.....

messages.author: 68ce5dd269fd758c
messages.subject: Re: shiny server on Ubuntu package error
parts:
I guess this problem may due to the access authority of shiny server. 

Solution: 
1. Find the location where you install "tm"
2. check its authority with 'ls -l'
3. change its authority, e.g. sudo chmod 777 -R /dirctorytolibrarytm
4. restart shiny-server

Good luck.

messages.author: 2bf707539ac457df
messages.subject: Re: shiny server on Ubuntu package error
parts:
The issue has to do with the way R is installed on the server.  According to the instruction found here on rstudio wiki on github, R was installed under an ubuntu user who was logged in at the time, prior to shiny installation and shiny user creation.  The shiny server admin guide here doesn't also specify how to install R so that it is available to ALL users.  

This fixed my problem I run the following command to install tm package for "all" R user
sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('tm', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""


But to avoid the headache for others and have the correct procedure in place on gitbuh/admin guide, it is better to add a global R installation step prior shiny server installation. 

-G
